ideas.pitch: An offline-first mobile app using local LLMs and GPS traces to provide hazard and weather forecasting for hikers in the Peak District.
ideas.title: PeakDistrict TrailGuardian
ideas.why_it_could_win: Appeals directly to local judges in Sheffield by targeting a regional real-world safety problem using constrained on-device hardware.

ideas.pitch: Real-time commuter bottleneck predictor and alternative route optimizer for Sheffield Supertram and bus networks.
ideas.title: SteelCity TransitPulse
ideas.why_it_could_win: Focuses on immediate civic utility for Sheffield commuters, matching the practical demo-driven judging criteria seen in winning hacks.

ideas.pitch: A dashboard tracking local micro-generation and industrial power loads across South Yorkshire brownfield sites.
ideas.title: ForgeGrid Energy Tracker
ideas.why_it_could_win: Taps into regional industrial heritage and sustainability angles that resonate well with university hackathon judges in the North of England.

ideas.pitch: An interactive supply chain transparency map connecting independent Sheffield restaurants with local Yorkshire farms.
ideas.title: Sheffield LocalSourced
ideas.why_it_could_win: Features an immediately demonstrable UI and solves a hyper-local economic challenge with high visual appeal for judges.

ideas.pitch: Computer vision bouldering beta analyzer using pose estimation to grade movement efficiency on local climbing walls.
ideas.title: ClimbMetrics AI
ideas.why_it_could_win: Leverages difficult engineering (computer vision and biomechanics) which stood out strongly in previous hackathon winning projects.
